attempts.label: DANDI:001882
attempts.paper_title: Prevalence of IMPG1 and IMPG2 Mutations Leading to Retinitis Pigmentosa or Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy in a Cohort of Patients with Inherited Retinal Dystrophies
attempts.entry_title: IMPG1 and IMPG2 variants in retinal dystrophy patients (Yuan et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Yuan, Chatterjee, Leys, Odom and Salido (2025) on dandiset 001882, which holds a table of the seven patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 variants, a document of in silico tool outputs and the paper's four figures as image files. It checks the patients' genotypes, diagnoses and acuities, reads the phenotypes on the deposited figure panels, and retests the in silico findings (domains, pathogenicity scores, ClinVar, ProtParam values, gnomAD frequencies) with pinned outside services.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Yuan et al. (2025) from dandiset 001882

outcomes.statement: Of 480 IRD patients in the cohort, 7 (1.45%) carried IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations; 2 (0.41%) were diagnosed with RP and 5 (1.04%) with VMD.
outcomes.source: Results, opening paragraph (before 3.1)
outcomes.quote: In our study, 7 out of 480 patients with IRDs (1.45%) were found to have mutations in IMPG genes. Of these, two patients (0.41%) were diagnosed with RP, while five patients (1.04%) exhibited characteristics of VMD.
outcomes.notes: The spreadsheet holds 7 IMPG carriers (5 IMPG2, 2 IMPG1), 2 with RP (F32, M83) and 5 with VMD. Over the paper's cohort of 480 these are 1.458%, 0.417% and 1.042%, within 10% of 1.45%, 0.41% and 1.04% (and equal to them truncated to two decimals); 480/7 = 68.6, the Discussion's 1 in 68. The dandiset holds no patient outside the seven, so the denominator could not be checked.
deviations: The cohort size of 480 is taken from the paper (Methods 2.1), as the criterion allows when the dataset holds only the carriers; the second measured value is that number, not a measurement.

outcomes.statement: All seven patients with IMPG mutations were Caucasian.
outcomes.source: Results, opening paragraph (before 3.1)
outcomes.quote: All seven patients with IMPG mutations were Caucasian.
outcomes.notes: No file and no metadata field records race, ethnicity or ancestry; the spreadsheet's headers and the dandiset description were searched for race, ethnic, Caucasian, white, European and ancestry, with no hit.

outcomes.statement: The seven patients carry the variants of Table 1 (F32 IMPG1 c.2218C>T p.Leu740Phe heterozygous; M83 IMPG2 c.3056G>A p.Cys1019Tyr and c.391C>T p.Arg131Cys, compound heterozygous; M75 IMPG1 c.1269C>A p.Asp423Glu heterozygous; M82 IMPG2 c.745C>T p.Leu249Phe heterozygous; M73 and F57 IMPG2 c.2890C>T p.Arg964* heterozygous; M34 IMPG2 c.3262C>T p.Arg1088* heterozygous).
outcomes.source: Table 1; Results, opening paragraph (before 3.1)
outcomes.quote: All the patients are represented in Table 1.
outcomes.notes: All 7 patients match Table 1 in gene, cDNA change, protein change and zygosity (7 of 7, no field differs after normalising spaces around ';' and '&'). The spreadsheet writes F32's gene as IMPG1, where Table 1 prints IMGP1.
deviations: The spreadsheet looks like the authors' source for Table 1 (same patient labels and fields, with an extra column), so the test shows that the deposit agrees with the paper, not independent evidence of the clinical findings.

outcomes.statement: F32 (female, 32 years) has sectoral RP and M83 (male, 83) RP; M75 (male, 75), M82 (male, 82), M73 (male, 73), F57 (female, 57) and M34 (male, 34) have VMD.
outcomes.source: Table 1
outcomes.inferred: Sex, age and diagnosis per patient are read from Table 1 and the patient identifiers; no single sentence states them all.
outcomes.notes: Diagnoses match for 7 of 7 patients, compared with the spreadsheet's diagnosis column. Sex and age exist only in the patient label (F32 and so on), the label the paper uses, so their match (7 of 7) is true by construction and is not an independent measurement; no date of any kind is recorded, so the readings of age (at the last visit, or in 2024) cannot be told apart.
deviations: The spreadsheet looks like the authors' source for Table 1 (same patient labels and fields, with an extra column), so the test shows that the deposit agrees with the paper, not independent evidence of the clinical findings.

outcomes.statement: The RP mutations are all missense, dominant in IMPG1 and recessive (compound heterozygous) in IMPG2; all VMD mutations are dominant (heterozygous), either missense or nonsense.
outcomes.source: Results, opening paragraph (before 3.1); Figure 1; Table 1
outcomes.quote: Our findings show all missense mutations for the RP phenotype with dominant inheritance in IMPG1 and recessive in IMPG2 ... all patients expressing VMD harvest dominant mutations, which can be either mis- or non-sense
outcomes.notes: RP; both patients carry missense variants, F32 one IMPG1 variant marked D (dominant), M83 two IMPG2 variants marked R (recessive, 'Het for both genes'). VMD; all 5 carry one heterozygous variant marked D, 2 missense and 3 nonsense.
deviations: The spreadsheet looks like the authors' source for Table 1 (same patient labels and fields, with an extra column), so the test shows that the deposit agrees with the paper, not independent evidence of the clinical findings.

outcomes.source: Table 1; Results, 3.1 and 3.2, the paragraph on each patient
outcomes.inferred: The values of all seven patients are in Table 1; the text of 3.1 and 3.2 repeats each patient's values in separate paragraphs.
outcomes.notes: All 14 eyes match Table 1. The spreadsheet holds one acuity per eye and no visit date, so the two readings of the criterion (most recent visit, any visit) coincide.
deviations: The spreadsheet looks like the authors' source for Table 1 (same patient labels and fields, with an extra column), so the test shows that the deposit agrees with the paper, not independent evidence of the clinical findings.

outcomes.statement: Patient F32 has sector RP of the inferior retina; FF shows inferior sectoral bone spicule pigmentation, FAF reduced autofluorescence, SD-OCT a normal foveal architecture without significant thinning, and GVF a superior depression in both eyes.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.1 RP Patients, paragraph on Patient F32; Figure 2A,B
outcomes.quote: Clinically, Patient F32 presented with sector RP primarily affecting the inferior retina ( Figure 2 A,B). ... The FF examination revealed dystrophy of the inferior retina, characterized by sectorial bone spicule pigmentation (yellow arrows). The FAF imaging showed reduced autofluorescence corresponding to a superior visual field defect in both eyes
outcomes.notes: All 4 features are visible in both eyes on the Figure 2A,B panels; spicule pigment in the lower nasal periphery on FF, a matching band of reduced FAF with a sharp border, a normal fovea with a continuous ellipsoid zone on the B-scan, and a Goldmann field whose outer isopter reaches about 40 to 45 degrees superiorly against about 70 inferiorly.
deviations: The dandiset holds the images only as the annotated, cropped panels of the paper's own figure (one image per modality and eye, one OCT B-scan per eye), not the clinical image files; the test checks the text against the published figure, not against independent data.
Each feature was judged by the author's visual reading of the panels at full resolution, the only method the criterion allows; the readings are printed with the panels they rest on.

outcomes.statement: Patient M83 has bilateral outer retinal atrophy sparing the central fovea with a bull's eye pattern, 360 degree bone spicules, pale discs and attenuated vessels on FF; reduced FAF; an inferior residual crescent and small central field on GVF; and diffuse ellipsoid zone and outer nuclear layer loss on SD-OCT, sparing part of the central fovea in the left eye.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.1 RP Patients, paragraph on Patient M83; Figure 2C,D
outcomes.quote: The FF revealed bilateral outer retinal atrophy sparing the central fovea, with a bull's eye pattern surrounding the fovea ( Figure 2 C,D). ... The GVF demonstrated an inferior residual crescent in both eyes and a small central visual field. The SD-OCT shows diffuse loss of the ellipsoid zone and outer nuclear layer, sparing part of the central fovea in the left eye.
outcomes.notes: 6 of 9 named features are visible on the Figure 2C,D panels (atrophy, the bull's eye ring in the inset of the left eye, reduced FAF, the central island and inferior crescent on GVF, diffuse ellipsoid loss, and a spared segment in the left fovea). The 360-degree spread of bone spicules (the superior periphery is hidden by lashes), the pale discs and the attenuated vessels cannot be judged on the pseudo-colour widefield panels.
deviations: The dandiset holds the images only as the annotated, cropped panels of the paper's own figure (one image per modality and eye, one OCT B-scan per eye), not the clinical image files; the test checks the text against the published figure, not against independent data.

outcomes.statement: Patient M75 has bilateral subretinal vitelliform material in the macula on SD-OCT, macular hypopigmentation on FF, FAF hypo-autofluorescence in the right macula and hyper-autofluorescence in the left, early blockage and late window defects on FA, and a superior macular nevus.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.2 VMD Patients, paragraph on Patient M75; Figure 3A,B
outcomes.quote: Subretinal vitelliform material was detected bilaterally in the macula by SD-OCT ( Figure 3 A,B). The FF shows hypopigmentation in the macula of both eyes. Hypo-autofluorescence, suggesting retinal atrophy, was observed in the right macula, while hyper-autofluorescence, indicative of vitelliform deposits, was noted in the left macula using FAF.
outcomes.notes: 5 of 6 features are visible on the Figure 3A,B panels. SD-OCT shows subfoveal material in both eyes; FF a small pale foveal lesion in both; FAF a dark right macula (mean 0.75 of the surround at r16, 95th percentile 0.90) and a bright focus in the left (95th percentile 1.37 of the surround, maximum brighter than in 97% of the background discs, bright under all five readings), so the left macula is hyper-autofluorescent as the text says, not hypo-autofluorescent as the legend says; the nevus is seen above the left fovea on infrared and FF, not in the right eye. The dandiset holds one angiogram frame per eye, so the early blockage and the late window defects cannot both be seen.
deviations: The dandiset holds the images only as the annotated, cropped panels of the paper's own figure (one image per modality and eye, one OCT B-scan per eye), not the clinical image files; the test checks the text against the published figure, not against independent data.

outcomes.statement: Patient M82 has late-stage VMD with foveal atrophy; SD-OCT shows an attenuated ellipsoid and retinal thinning in the right eye and a vitelliform lesion with small ellipsoid disruption in the left; FF shows foveal hypopigmentation and FA window defects in both eyes.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.2 VMD Patients, paragraph on Patient M82; Figure 3C,D
outcomes.quote: SD-OCT of the right eye showed attenuated ellipsoid and retinal thinning, while the left eye displayed a vitelliform lesion with a small ellipsoid zone disruption. The FF shows hypopigmentation of the fovea in both eyes. The FFA demonstrates a bilateral window defect.

On FF the fovea is mottled with no clear pale area, and on FA the left arrowed area is not brighter than its surround (small hyperfluorescent dots are seen in the right eye). The FAF panels are empty (NA, 3 to 4% non-black pixels), as the legend says.

outcomes.statement: Patient M73 has bilateral macular subretinal hyporeflective spaces and ellipsoid disruption on SD-OCT, foveal hypopigmentation, dot-blot hemorrhages and peripheral cobblestone degeneration on FF, and bilateral hyper-autofluorescence on FAF.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.2 VMD Patients, paragraph on Patient M73; Figure 3E,F
outcomes.quote: Patient M73, a 73-year-old male, presented with bilaterally macular subretinal hyporeflective spaces on SD-OCT, suggesting the reabsorption of vitelliform material ( Figure 3 E,F). Additional findings included ellipsoid disruption.
outcomes.notes: 4 of 6 features are visible on the Figure 3E,F panels; subretinal hyporeflective spaces in both eyes, the ellipsoid break in the right eye, a small pale foveal lesion and peripheral cobblestone patches in both eyes. FAF shows a bright focus in the left macula (maximum 1.49 of the surround, above every background disc) and in the right only a small speck (maximum 1.11, 95th percentile 1.02) that is no brighter than the perimacular ring (64% of background discs are as bright), so under the adopted reading the hyper-autofluorescence is seen in one eye, not both. Two of the four other readings count the right eye too (95th percentile above 1.0 of the surround; above 1.1 of the adjacent macula, 1.21). Dot-blot hemorrhages cannot be told apart from pigment, on the downsampled panels or on the full-resolution crops, so the outcome is partial under every reading (5 of 6 at most) and does not rest on the choice of reading.
deviations: The dandiset holds the images only as the annotated, cropped panels of the paper's own figure (one image per modality and eye, one OCT B-scan per eye), not the clinical image files; the test checks the text against the published figure, not against independent data.
Each feature was judged by the author's visual reading of the panels at full resolution, the only method the criterion allows; the readings are printed with the panels they rest on.

FAF features are also measured at the lesion the yellow arrow marks, with the arrow pixels left out (mean in discs of radius 16, 32 and 48 pixels, 95th percentile and maximum within 16 pixels, darker area within 100 pixels, each against the median of an annulus 80 to 140 pixels out, and 36 background discs of radius 16 placed 110 pixels from the lesion, inside the surround annulus, so on the perimacular ring, not the general fundus); the lesion centres, radii and the 0.85 cut-off are a standard choice made to make the reading checkable, not the paper's method, and every radius is shown.

Not an assumption the outcome rests on, since the outcome is partial under every reading. Neither the paper nor the claims file says what makes a lesion hyper-autofluorescent; the paper graded by inspection. Five readings of a bright focus are run on every eye (95th percentile above 1.1 or 1.0 of the surround, above 1.1 of the adjacent macula, and 95th percentile or maximum brighter than in 95% of same-size background discs of the same panel, which lie on the perimacular ring). The last is adopted, since hyper-autofluorescence is a lesion brighter than the fundus around it, and it calibrates brighter on the panel's own perimacular ring while keeping a small focus. The readings agree on every eye except M73's right (bright under the 1.0 surround and the macula readings, not under the other three) and M73's left (not bright under the background 95th percentile reading).

outcomes.statement: Both RP patients have superior visual field limitation (inferior retina affected first), and neither has cystoid maculopathy.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 3 (on Patient M83 and the RP patients)
outcomes.quote: Both RP patients experienced visual field limitations in the superior visual field. ... Cystoid maculopathy did not occur in either young or old patients.
outcomes.notes: Both RP patients have a superior field limitation on the Goldmann charts (F32 an outer isopter at about 40 to 45 degrees superiorly against 70 inferiorly; M83 no field above the central island, with an inferior residual crescent), and none of the 4 B-scans shows intraretinal cystoid spaces. Only one B-scan per eye is in the dandiset, so cysts elsewhere in the macula cannot be excluded.

outcomes.statement: In most VMD patients visual acuity was not significantly reduced; the only exception is M73 (20/100 OD, 20/50 OS).
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, in most VMD patients, visual acuity was not significantly reduced. The only exception is patient M73, who has a BCVA of 20/100 OD and 20/50 OS.
outcomes.notes: VMD acuities, worse and better eye; M75 20/40 and 20/40, M82 20/30 and 20/25, M73 20/100 and 20/50, F57 and M34 20/20. Under all four readings of the criterion (better eye worse than 20/40; worse eye worse than 20/40, 20/50 or 20/70) M73 is the only patient counted as reduced, and the other 4 are not.

outcomes.statement: The two unrelated carriers of IMPG2 p.Arg964* (M73 and F57) have similar vitelliform macular lesions, but the older (M73) has peripheral cobblestone lesions and macular lesions with increased autofluorescence.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: Both patients have similar vitelliform macular lesions. However, the oldest patient (M73) presents with peripheral cobblestone lesions, and the macular lesions have increased autofluorescence.
outcomes.notes: Both patients have subfoveal vitelliform lesions on SD-OCT (M73 hyporeflective spaces, F57 hyperreflective deposits), and M73 alone has peripheral cobblestone patches on FF (F57's images show less periphery). On FAF M73's left macula has a bright focus (maximum 1.49 of the surround, above every background disc) where F57 has none in either eye (100% and 97% of background discs are as bright), but under the adopted reading M73's right macula has none either (64% of background discs are as bright), so the increased autofluorescence holds in one of his two eyes. Under two of the other readings his right eye is bright too, and all three parts of the criterion would hold. The criterion gives no rule for a partial result; partially reproduced is used because two of its three parts hold and the third holds in one eye.

outcomes.statement: Patient M73, who also carries a BEST1 variant, had a normal EOG, which the authors read as against Best disease.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 5 (on Patient M73)
outcomes.quote: However, the patient's EOG results were normal, a finding inconsistent with Best disease but more indicative of IMPG2-associated retinal dystrophy.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no EOG; none of EOG, electro-oculogram or Arden occurs in any of its text (spreadsheet, Word document, folder script, metadata), and no file is an electrophysiology recording.

outcomes.statement: Besides their IMPG variants, F32 carries a JAG1 variant, M73 a BEST1 variant, and M83 heterozygous variants of uncertain significance in ALMS1, CEP164, COL11A1, CPLANE1, EYS, KIF7, NPHP4 and PHYH.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraphs 2, 3 and 5
outcomes.quote: It is also important to note that this patient had two diseased gene variants ... IMPG1 and JAG1 .
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no genetic report beyond the IMPG variants of the spreadsheet; none of JAG1, BEST1, ALMS1, CEP164, COL11A1, CPLANE1, EYS, KIF7, NPHP4 or PHYH occurs in any of its text.

outcomes.statement: The variants lie in or near named protein domains. In IMPG1, p.Leu740Phe is near (3.1) or in (3.5, Discussion) the EGF-like domain next to SEA2, and p.Asp423Glu is between SEA1 and SEA2. In IMPG2, p.Arg131Cys is near SEA-1, p.Leu249Phe in SEA1, p.Arg964* in SEA2, p.Cys1019Tyr in the EGF-1-like domain and p.Arg1088* in the EGF-like 2 domain.
outcomes.source: Figure 1; Results, 3.1 and 3.2, the paragraph on each patient; Results, 3.5
outcomes.quote: He is heterozygous for the p.Cys1019Tyr mutation in one allele, which affects the EGF-1-like domain, and the p.Arg131Cys mutation in the other allele, which is located near the non-proteolytic SEA-1 domain.
outcomes.notes: No reading places all 7; UniProt, InterPro and the PROSITE profiles place 6, Pfam and SMART 4. UniProt (Q17R60 v129, Q9BZV3 v146); IMPG1 has only SEA 1 (232-354) and SEA 2 (571-684), no EGF-like domain, so p.Leu740Phe cannot be near one; the other 6 hold. InterPro 110.0 and PROSITE profiles; IMPG1 has an EGF-like domain at 684-722, 18 residues before Leu740 (near, the closest domain, not in it), but IMPG2 has a single EGF-like domain (1010-1051), so p.Arg1088* lies in no EGF-like 2 domain; the other 6 hold. Pfam 38.2 and SMART 9.0 annotate only the two SEA domains of each protein, so p.Leu740Phe, p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Arg1088* fail. p.Arg131Cys is 108 residues from SEA1 and 109 from the end of the signal peptide (1-22), so 'near SEA-1' rests on one residue if the signal peptide counts as a domain. The paper's own 'in' for p.Leu740Phe holds under no reading. The spreadsheet's 'Location of Variant' column places p.Leu740Phe 'Post EGF-like 1', after the domain.
deviations: UniProt entries are pinned through UniSave at the versions current in November 2024 (Q17R60 v129 and Q9BZV3 v146, both released 2 October 2024 and replaced on 27 November 2024, as cell 61 prints); InterPro is read from its current release (110.0), which cannot be pinned through its API.

outcomes.statement: In silico tools predict all IMPG2 variants and the novel IMPG1 p.Asp423Glu to be pathogenic, and IMPG1 p.Leu740Phe to be likely benign, with the scores of Table 2.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.3 Pathogenicity Prediction; Table 2
outcomes.quote: In IMPG1, the novel variant p.Asp423Glu is predicted to be pathogenic, while the known variant p.Leu740Phe is considered likely benign.
outcomes.notes: SIFT and PolyPhen-2 HumVar (Ensembl VEP release 116, MANE Select transcripts) match Table 2 exactly for the three IMPG2 missense variants (SIFT 0, 0, 0; PolyPhen 0.996, 0.645, 0.998) but not for IMPG1; VEP gives SIFT 0.02 for p.Leu740Phe and 0.09 for p.Asp423Glu, the paper's two values exchanged, and PolyPhen 0.106 and 0.043 (paper 0.575 and 0.98). PolyPhen-2 HumDiv (dbNSFP 4.8a) gives 0.575 for p.Leu740Phe as the paper does, 3 of 5 values within tolerance, but 0.31 for p.Asp423Glu. VEP calls p.Asp423Glu tolerated (SIFT) and benign (PolyPhen), against the paper's Pathogenic, so the Prediction column is not matched. CADD PHRED matches at most 2 of 7 values under any of GRCh37 or GRCh38 and v1.6 or v1.7; the nonsense variants score 36 to 45 against 11.2 and 13.4. No FATHMM, FATHMM-MKL or FATHMM-XF coding score and no MutationTaster score in dbNSFP matches the paper's columns (0 of 5 and 0 of 7), under any value of dbNSFP's per-transcript or per-model lists; the FATHMM-MKL web server gives the same coding scores as dbNSFP (0.83 to 0.99 for the IMPG2 variants, against 0.0076 to 0.0577) and matches 0 of 5, coding or non-coding. The MutationTaster2021 API redirects to the GeneCascade home page, even for its own documented example, so the paper's 0 to 100 MutationTaster score could not be recomputed. The paper's ids for p.Leu740Phe and p.Arg964* (rs15048636, rs267606975) differ from the variants' ids (rs150486366, rs267606875); the dandiset's Word document gives rs267606875.
deviations: The web tools of November 2024 cannot be called in a pinned version. SIFT and PolyPhen-2 HumVar come from Ensembl VEP (release 116); PolyPhen-2 HumDiv, FATHMM and MutationTaster from dbNSFP 4.8a (MyVariant.info build 20250624), whose MutationTaster score is a probability, not the paper's 0 to 100 score; FATHMM-MKL also from the FATHMM web server as it answers today; CADD from its versioned API.
dbNSFP's per-transcript lists (SIFT, FATHMM) cannot always be lined up with its transcript list, since MyVariant.info drops missing entries; every list value is shown and a match by any value counts.
MutationTaster2021, which gives a 0 to 100 tree vote, was tried through its API and does not answer.
SIFT and PolyPhen-2 were not run on GRCh37 in the notebook; VEP's GRCh37 service took 12 minutes while preparing (not run here).

outcomes.statement: IMPG1 p.Asp423Glu, found in M75, is a novel variant with no ClinVar entry, and its association with VMD is reported here for the first time.
outcomes.source: Table 2 (Existing Variant ID column); Discussion, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Notably, patient M75 harbored a novel missense mutation, p.Asp423Glu, in IMPG1, marking its first reported association with VMD.
outcomes.notes: IMPG1 c.1269C>A on NM_001563.4 is GRCh38 6:76002940 G>T (rs758038128). It is ClinVar variation 1000102, NM_001563.4(IMPG1):c.1269C>A (p.Asp423Glu), a missense variant of uncertain significance in IMPG1, in all 4 ClinVar VCF releases of November 2024 (3, 11, 20 and 26 November). It first appears in the release of 15 March 2021 (the release of 8 March 2021 lacks it), from one submission last evaluated on 28 August 2020, with the condition 'not provided'; so ClinVar records no association with VMD, and the claim's second half (first association with VMD) is not contradicted. The same position also carries a synonymous G>A record (1156378).

outcomes.statement: All five missense variants are predicted to destabilize the protein by every tool (all ΔΔG negative), and p.Leu249Phe shows the largest destabilizing effect.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.4 Prediction of Protein Stability for Point Mutations; Table 3
outcomes.quote: Our analysis revealed that all the variants, including p.Leu740Phe, p.Asp423Glu, p.Cys1019Tyr, p.Leu249Phe, and p.Arg131Cys, lead to destabilizing effects on the proteins ... Specifically, the p.Leu249Phe variant exhibited the largest destabilizing effect
outcomes.notes: Tested on the two sequence-based tools; the 15 values of mCSM, SDM and DUET need the I-TASSER models of Methods 2.3, which are not deposited. MuPRO (web server, sequence only) gives a negative DDG for all 5 variants and matches Table 3 for 3 of 5 (p.Leu740Phe -0.930, p.Asp423Glu -0.478, p.Arg131Cys -0.627); it gives p.Cys1019Tyr -0.887 (Table 3 -1.266) and p.Leu249Phe -1.2666 (Table 3 -1.525), so Table 3's p.Cys1019Tyr value is MuPRO's p.Leu249Phe value, which the Word document gives for p.Leu249Phe. I-Mutant 2.0 (web server, sequence, 25 C, pH 7) gives a positive, stabilizing DDG for 4 of 5 (p.Leu740Phe +0.19, p.Asp423Glu +0.88, p.Cys1019Tyr +0.14, p.Leu249Phe +0.55) and -1.22 for p.Arg131Cys; for IMPG2 these are Table 3's magnitudes (0.14, 0.55) with the sign reversed, and -1.22 is the Word document's value (Table 3 -1.13). Its sign classifier calls p.Asp423Glu an increase in stability (reliability 8 of 10). So under either I-Mutant output not every variant is destabilizing by every tool, and the claim's first part fails on a tool the paper names. The ranking cannot be tested on all five tools; p.Leu249Phe is the most destabilizing under MuPRO and p.Arg131Cys under I-Mutant. On Table 3's own values every entry is negative and p.Leu249Phe has the most negative mean (-1.25). The Word document holds 23 of the 25 values; 20 agree within 10%, and it gives SDM +0.58 (Stabilizing) for p.Asp423Glu where Table 3 prints -0.52. The outcome rests on the claims file's reading that iMutant is run from sequence; the paper does not name the mode, neither sequence output gives Table 3's IMPG1 values (-0.85, -0.76), and the regression and the classifier disagree in sign for p.Leu740Phe, p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Leu249Phe, so the paper may have used the structure mode on the undeposited models (asked of a reader in questions/001882.yaml).
deviations: mCSM, SDM and DUET were not run: they need the I-TASSER models, which are not deposited, and a rerun of I-TASSER (a queued web server with stochastic output) was not tried. 15 of the 25 values are therefore not computed.

MuPRO and I-Mutant 2.0 were run on their web servers as they answer today (no version can be pinned), on the UniProt sequences Q17R60 v129 and Q9BZV3 v146, the criterion's reading; I-Mutant at its default 25 C and pH 7, in both its DDG regression and sign classifier modes.

Assumption. iMutant is run from sequence, as the criterion says. The paper does not say so; Methods 2.4 gives only the server's address, its reference 46 is 'I-Mutant2.0, Predicting stability changes upon mutation from the protein sequence or structure', and Methods 2.3 built I-TASSER models 'for further analysis'. The structure mode cannot be run, since the models are not deposited, so the outcome rests on the sequence reading and on one tool, in one mode, on a server with no version. Under MuPRO alone every value is negative.

outcomes.statement: In IMPG1, neither p.Asp423Glu nor p.Leu740Phe changes hydrogen bonds, van der Waals interactions or polar contacts significantly.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.5, paragraph 1; Figure 4A,B
outcomes.quote: In IMPG1, no significant differences were observed in hydrogen bonds, van der Waals interactions or polar contacts between the reference and mutant proteins.
outcomes.notes: DynaMut needs the I-TASSER models of Methods 2.3, which are not deposited anywhere; a rerun of I-TASSER (a queued web server with stochastic output, the claims file's only reading) was not tried. The dandiset holds the residue-contact images of Figure 4A,B only.

outcomes.statement: In IMPG2, p.Cys1019Tyr replaces the polar bond of Cys1019 with Ser1023 and its hydrogen bond with Cys1036 by new bonds with Ser1023, Gln1017 and Cys1025; p.Leu249Phe loses the hydrogen bonds of Leu249 with Val305, Lys252, Leu373 and Val307; p.Arg131Cys loses the hydrogen bond with Tyr134 and a van der Waals interaction.
outcomes.source: Results, 3.5, paragraphs 3 to 5; Figure 4C to 4E
outcomes.quote: In the reference protein, Cysteine 1019 interacts with Serine 1023 through polar bonds and with Cysteine 1036 via hydrogen bonds ( Figure 4 C). In the mutant protein, Tyrosine 1019 replaces Cysteine 1019, disrupting these original interactions. Instead, Tyrosine 1019 forms new bonds with Serine 1023, Glutamine 1017, and Cysteine 1025.
outcomes.notes: As for impg1-interactions-unchanged. The dandiset holds the residue-contact images of Figure 4C-E; in that file the images of the top row show Arg131 and Cys131 and the middle row Cys1019 and Tyr1019, while the labels beside them read p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Leu249Phe (read by eye).

outcomes.statement: ProtParam gives reference IMPG1 a molecular weight of 89,387 Da, pI 4.79, instability index 53.57 and aliphatic index 75.63; p.Asp423Glu raises the weight (89,419), pI (4.81) and instability index (53.76), and p.Leu740Phe raises the weight (89,421) and lowers the aliphatic index (75.14).
outcomes.source: Results, 3.5, paragraph 2; Table 4
outcomes.quote: The molecular weight increased from 89.387 KDa in the reference protein to 89.419 KDa in the p.Asp423Glu mutant and 89.421 KDa in the p.Leu740Phe mutant
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), the full UniProt sequence (Q17R60 v129, 797 residues), gives 14 of 18 values; all 6 of the reference (89,387.4 Da, pI 4.793, 12,450 atoms, instability 53.57, aliphatic 75.63, GRAVY -0.482) and all 6 of p.Leu740Phe, and the instability (53.76) and aliphatic (75.63) indices of p.Asp423Glu. Its weight (89,401.4 against 89,419), pI (4.796 against 4.81), atoms (12,453 against 12,457) and GRAVY (-0.482 against -0.474) do not match; an Asp to Phe change at 423 gives Table 4's p.Asp423Glu column (89,419.5, 4.81, 12,457, 53.76, 75.63, -0.474). The directions the text states all hold. Reading (b), without the signal peptide, matches no value. The pI is computed with Biopython's Bjellqvist pK values, not ExPASy's own code; the reference matches (4.793), and Asp to Glu moves it by +0.003 where Table 4 moves it by +0.02 (Asp to Phe, +0.017), so a small difference between the codes would not bring 4.796 to 4.81.
deviations: Values are computed with ProtParam's definitions (ExPASy average residue masses, the Bjellqvist pK values and the instability index as Biopython implements ProtParam, the Ikai aliphatic index, Kyte-Doolittle GRAVY) in place of the web tool.

outcomes.statement: In gnomAD, IMPG2 p.Cys1019Tyr occurs in about 1 in 93,300 European (non-Finnish) individuals; p.Arg131Cys in about 1 in 4100 European (non-Finnish) and 1 in 3000 Middle Eastern; p.Arg964* in about 1 in 18,700 African/African American and 1 in 59,000 European (non-Finnish); and IMPG1 p.Leu740Phe in about 1 in 332 European (non-Finnish).
outcomes.source: Results, 3.1 RP Patients, paragraph on Patient M83; Results, 3.2 VMD Patients, paragraph on M73 and F57; Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The Cys1019Tyr variant is a rare mutation found exclusively in the European (non-Finnish) population, with an estimated frequency of approximately 1 in 93,300 individuals.
outcomes.notes: Under gnomAD v4.1 joint allele counts with '1 in N' read as 1/(2 x allele frequency) (one carrier in N individuals), all 6 values are within 10%; 1 in 98,335 (p.Cys1019Tyr, 6 of 1,180,016 European non-Finnish alleles), 4,096 and 3,031 (p.Arg131Cys, European non-Finnish and Middle Eastern), 18,722 and 58,997 (p.Arg964*, African/African American and European non-Finnish) and 332 (p.Leu740Phe). v4.1 exomes match 4 of 6; v4.1 genomes, v3.1.2 genomes and the 1/allele frequency reading match none. p.Cys1019Tyr is absent from v3.1.2.
deviations: The paper names no gnomAD version; the readings of the criterion were run and one combination matches all values. The gnomAD API prints no release number; that gnomad_r4 is v4.1 comes from gnomAD's documentation, not from an output of the notebook.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds no clinical recording. The fundus photographs, FAF, angiograms, OCT and Goldmann fields exist only as the annotated, cropped panels of the paper's Figures 2 and 3 (one image per modality and eye, one OCT B-scan per eye, a single angiogram frame per eye). The EOG of patient M73, the genetic panel reports (the JAG1, BEST1 and other variants the Discussion cites), race or ethnicity, visit dates and any record of the other 473 patients of the cohort are not in it.

The first column of the spreadsheet 'derivatives/small table for 7 patients 20241127.xlsx' holds what look like hospital record numbers of the seven patients, in a public CC0 dataset. The attempt did not print or use them.

The metadata give 1 subject, 4 samples and no species, approach or measurement technique, while the files describe seven human patients. The figure files are named as BIDS microscopy samples (sub-01/micr/sub-01_sample-0N_microscopy.ome.tif.tif, one .ome.tif.jpg) but are RGB figure exports from Adobe Illustrator, not OME-TIFF and not microscopy; one is named 'Fig 3. VMD 20241122.1-01.tif'.

The paper is named only in the description, not in relatedResource. No file describes the spreadsheet's columns (the 'Location of Variant' column is not in the paper; Refraction, clinVar and Pathogenicity are empty) or says which figure each image file is.
Five identical Google Drive desktop.ini files and the script setup_bids.py, which only makes the folder layout and a dataset_description.json that is not deposited, are among the 13 assets.

The Word document 'sourcedata/protein structure and stabilityIMPG2 TABLE original.docx' differs from the paper's Table 3. Of the 23 Table 3 values it holds, 3 differ by more than 10%; SDM gives p.Asp423Glu +0.58 (Stabilizing) where Table 3 prints -0.52, MuPRO gives p.Leu249Phe -1.2666 where Table 3 prints -1.525, and mCSM gives p.Asp423Glu -0.58 against -0.653. Three more differ within 10% (SDM p.Cys1019Tyr -0.85 against -0.78, iMutant p.Arg131Cys -1.22 against -1.13, DUET p.Leu249Phe -1.777 against -1.77). It has no iMutant value for IMPG1. Its Table A names p.Leu249Phe 'p.Leu 249Tyr'. Rerun here, MuPRO gives -1.2666 for p.Leu249Phe (the document's value) and -0.887 for p.Cys1019Tyr, where both the document and Table 3 give -1.266, and I-Mutant 2.0 gives -1.22 for p.Arg131Cys (the document's value).

Table 4's p.Asp423Glu column (89,419 Da, pI 4.81, 12,457 atoms, GRAVY -0.474) is what ProtParam's definitions give for Asp423Phe on UniProt Q17R60, not for Asp423Glu (89,401.4 Da, 4.796, 12,453, -0.482); a single Asp to Glu change adds one CH2.

In Table 2 the IMPG1 SIFT scores match VEP's values for the two variants exchanged (p.Leu740Phe 0.02, p.Asp423Glu 0.09), and two variant ids are mistyped (rs15048636 for rs150486366, rs267606975 for rs267606875, which the dandiset's Word document gives).

IMPG1 p.Asp423Glu (c.1269C>A, GRCh38 6:76002940 G>T, rs758038128), which the paper calls novel, was ClinVar variation 1000102 (missense, uncertain significance, condition not provided) in every ClinVar release from 15 March 2021, including all of November 2024.

In the Figure 4 file of IMPG2 (sub-01_sample-04b) the variant labels are one row out of step with the images; the top row shows Arg131 and Cys131 and is labelled p.Cys1019Tyr, the middle row shows Cys1019 and Tyr1019 and is labelled p.Leu249Phe (read by eye).

Question for the paper's authors. Which PolyPhen-2 model (HumDiv or HumVar), which FATHMM model (the 'FATHMM coding' column) and which MutationTaster output (the 0 to 100 'score') give Table 2, on which transcript and genome build, and which CADD version; which gnomAD version and which reading of '1 in N' (the values match v4.1 joint counts as 1/(2 x allele frequency)); and which source gives the domain boundaries of Figure 1, whose IMPG1 EGF-like domain is not in UniProt and whose IMPG2 EGF-like 2 domain is not in InterPro. Also, which I-Mutant 2.0 output and sign give Table 3's iMutant column, and what made a fundus autofluorescence lesion count as hyper-autofluorescent (the right eye of M73, whose lesion holds only a speck no brighter than the background fundus).

Table 3's iMutant values for IMPG2 p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Leu249Phe (-0.14, -0.55, destabilizing) are the magnitudes the I-Mutant 2.0 server the paper names gives from sequence with the sign reversed (+0.14, +0.55, which the server prints as increased stability); the server also gives +0.19 and +0.88 for the IMPG1 variants (Table 3 -0.85 and -0.76), and its sign classifier calls p.Asp423Glu stabilizing. Table 3's MuPRO value for p.Cys1019Tyr (-1.266) is the one MuPRO gives for p.Leu249Phe.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the DANDI API only, and could not run the FAF measures. It gave its own outcome for each claim; all 26 agree with the record's outcomes then (for table3-destabilizing and the two interaction claims it gave blocked as data_missing where the record had not_runnable). Its other points: the dataset's figures are the paper's own published panels and its spreadsheet is the authors' source file for Table 1, so 'reproduced' for the dataset claims means the deposit agrees with the paper, not independent evidence (problem 1); the Table 2 inconsistencies (problem 4); the dandiset metadata gives 1 subject and no species (problem 10); the 2 images of the Word document were not shown. In reply the Word document's images are shown, and problems 1, 4 and 10 were already stated in the deviations and findings.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 26 outcomes as recorded, with a reservation on table3-destabilizing. Its other points; the count of desktop.ini files is five, not six (cells 0, 9, 10, the summary and the finding); the summary's account of the Word document's differences from Table 3; the unprinted statements that the draft holds the same 13 assets, that the UniSave versions were current in November 2024 and that gnomad_r4 serves v4.1; and the record's narrowing of its round-1 problem 1. In reply the count is corrected to five everywhere (cell 3 and cell 9 now print it), cell 3 compares the draft's assets with the published version's (13, the same paths, sizes and asset ids), the Word document's differences are restated from cell 70, and the points tied to a claim are answered under that claim. No outcome changed and none is proposed.

entries.name: 001882-yuan-2025
entries.title: IMPG1 and IMPG2 variants in retinal dystrophy patients (Yuan et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Yuan, Chatterjee, Leys, Odom and Salido (2025) on dandiset 001882, which holds a table of the seven patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 variants, a document of in silico tool outputs and the paper's four figures as image files. It checks the patients' genotypes, diagnoses and acuities, reads the phenotypes on the deposited figure panels, and retests the in silico findings (domains, pathogenicity scores, ClinVar, ProtParam values, gnomAD frequencies) with pinned outside services.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Yuan et al. (2025) from dandiset 001882
